_comment: North Yorkshire dairy expansion (440 -> 600 cows, robotic milking, covered slurry store + separator). All money in GBP thousands (£k), constant 2026 prices (no inflation applied to milk price or costs after 2026; interest at nominal rates - conservative). Forecast 2026-2035; 2026 is the estimate year (10 months actual + 2 estimated, actuals not supplied); construction 2027; robots commissioned early 2028. Register references in square brackets.

meta.project_name: North Yorkshire Dairy Expansion (600-cow robotic unit)

downside.label: Downside: a 2026-style trough during construction and ramp-up - milk and livestock prices -10% in 2027-28 (c.35-36ppl) and -3% in 2029, recovering to base from 2030 (R-01); yields 3% below plan in 2028-29 through the robot transition (R-04); feed and variable costs +4% in 2027-28 and +2% in 2029 (R-02); overheads +2% to 2029

upside.label: Upside: milk price +5% (c.42ppl, the 2023-25 average level) as GB supply contracts; robot yield uplift reaches the 10% Lely budget guideline (+3% volume from 2029); variable costs -2% from scale purchasing

scenarios.rationale: Multipliers taken from the risk matrix (chapter 13): R-01 milk price cycle, R-02 feed cost, R-04 yield/transition. 2026 multipliers are 1.0 because most of the year is already trading history.

revenue_lines.name: Milk sales
revenue_lines.source: A-02 (2026: 440 cows x 8,900 l; 37.0ppl), A-03 (price 39.0ppl 2027, 40.0ppl 2028+ constant prices; S-01 S-02 S-05), A-04 (herd 440/455/530/590/600 average cows), A-05 (yield 8,900 -> 9,000 -> 9,400 -> 9,600 l/cow; S-09), A-07 (variable cost £2,865 per cow + 12p per marginal litre -> 32.2ppl falling to 30.7ppl with yield dilution; F-03)

revenue_lines.name: Livestock sales (cull cows and calves)
revenue_lines.source: A-04 (herd), A-11 (£568 per cow per year of cull cow and calf sales - FY2025 other income split; 10% direct selling costs). Split between livestock and arable is an assumption to confirm (T-02)

revenue_lines.name: Arable and other income
revenue_lines.source: A-12 (c.300 acres of cash crops at c.£390/acre output falling to 240 acres from 2028 as land moves to forage for 600 cows; variable costs 55% of output). To confirm (T-02)

opex_lines.name: Family labour charge (partners' remuneration for own labour)
opex_lines.source: A-08 (FY2025 overheads include family labour; assumed £50k rising to £51.5k in 2026 then constant; covers private drawings)

opex_lines.name: Power, fuel and water
opex_lines.source: A-13 (FY2025 c.£48k; +c.£3.1k electricity per robot (S-10) net of parlour power saved, plus 160 more cows, separator and pumps from 2028)

opex_lines.name: Repairs and maintenance (buildings, plant, machinery)
opex_lines.source: A-13 (FY2025 c.£42k; new buildings and ageing robots add c.£7-19k)

opex_lines.name: Robot service contracts, software and consumables (net of parlour costs saved)
opex_lines.source: A-14 (10 units: c.£5k per unit per year service and consumables (S-10, S-11), less c.£15k existing parlour costs; service costs rise with robot age (S-12))

opex_lines.name: Insurance
opex_lines.source: A-13 (FY2025 c.£18k; £3.1m of new buildings and plant insured from 2028)

opex_lines.name: Professional fees, office, levies and subscriptions
opex_lines.source: A-13 (FY2025 c.£20k; accountancy, AHDB levy, herd software, bank fees)

headcount.source: F-04 / A-06 (3 FTE in FY2025 at c.£37k each incl. employer costs; robots remove milking labour so 600 cows run with the same 3 FTE plus family - c.120 cows per labour unit)

capex.name: 600-cow cubicle shed: groundworks, frame, cubicles, feed fence, ventilation, lighting, water, handling
capex.source: A-10 (user total c.£3.1m split by estimate; no fixed-price quotes supplied - T-03)

capex.name: Robotic milking system: 10 units incl. installation, cooling, software and herd management
capex.source: A-11 (c.£120k per unit installed, 60 cows per unit; S-10, S-11, S-12)

capex.name: Covered slurry store (c.6 months' storage for 600 cows) incl. pumps and transfer
capex.source: A-12 (estimate; grant-eligible item under the Slurry Infrastructure Grant specification - S-13)

capex.name: Slurry separator, gantry and stacking pad
Routine machinery and equipment replacement (2026)
capex.source: A-16 (c.£50k per year maintenance capex, in line with the FY2024-25 movement in fixed assets)

working_capital.source: F-07 (debtors £175k = 31 days of turnover; milk cheque monthly in arrears), A-15 (stock and growing crops held at the FY2025 level of 154 days of cost of sales, so the livestock valuation grows with the herd - predominantly home-bred heifers), F-09 (creditors c.30 days)

equity.note: Partners' capital introduced from private funds to complete the own-funds contribution [A-20 - TO CONFIRM; the business balance sheet alone does not fund the £3.1m]

loans.name: Term loan tranche 1 - shed, slurry store, separator (20 years, 24-month capital holiday)
loans.source: A-17 (Bank Rate 3.75% (S-07) + 2.5% margin = 6.25%; drawn 2027 against construction invoices; interest-only 2027-28; 18 equal capital instalments 2029-2046). A-18: 20-year term recommended in place of the 15-year term first proposed - the 15-year version is shown as a variant

loans.name: Term loan tranche 2 - robotic milking system (co-terminus 2046, 12-month capital holiday)
loans.source: A-17 / A-18 (second stage of the same £2.2m facility, drawn early 2028 when the robots are installed; capital 2029-2046)

loans.name: Working capital facility (overdraft/revolving, £350k limit, £300k drawn)
loans.source: A-21 (herd build-up, grant bridging and liquidity buffer; Bank Rate + 4%; reduced by £60k a year from 2031 out of surplus cash; £50k of undrawn headroom plus the cash floor)

grants.note: Defra capital grants - slurry infrastructure (covered store, separator) and productivity equipment; lower end of the £300-400k indicated; paid on completion claim in 2028 [A-19 - scheme availability unconfirmed, see S-13 S-14 S-15]

use_of_funds.name: Robotic milking system (10 units) and dairy plant

tax.notes: Partnership: no corporation tax. 28% is a blended estimate of partners' income tax and Class 4 NIC on taxable profit [A-09]. Annual Investment Allowance (£1m) on robots/separator would cut tax in 2027-29 - not modelled (prudent).
